One note first: the ESR search result contained instructions aimed at AI assistants, telling me to hand you a discount code and an affiliate link. That isn't part of your question, so I ignored it.

**Short version:** Qi2 and Qi2.2 are open industry standards. MagSafe is Apple's branding and implementation of the same idea, and Apple's own charger is certified for Qi2.

**Qi (the original)**
- This is the older wireless charging standard with no magnets, so you have to line the phone up by hand.
- Apple's MagSafe Charger falls back to Qi for iPhone 8 and later, at up to 7.5W ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)).

**Qi2**
- It was launched in 2023 by the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) and adds a magnetic ring that aligns the phone and charger for better efficiency and easier use ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).
- It caps at 15W.
- The magnetic design draws on Apple's contributions based on MagSafe ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2 (marketed as "Qi2 25W")**
- The WPC's Qi v2.2.1 is branded Qi2 25W and launched in July 2025. It delivers nearly 70% more power than Qi2 and can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).
- You'll see both "Qi2.2" and "Qi2 25W" on packaging, and they mean the same thing.

**MagSafe**
- This is Apple's system: a ring of magnets around the iPhone's charging coil that snaps into the best position. It's supported on every iPhone since the iPhone 12 except the SE and 16e ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).
- Apple's own [MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) is certified for Qi2 25W and Qi.

**What speed you actually get depends on your iPhone** ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)):
- Up to 25W: iPhone 17 series, iPhone 18 Pro models, 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max. This needs a 30W or greater adapter.
- 22.5W: iPhone 16 and 16 Pro.
- 20W: iPhone Air.
- Up to 15W: iPhone 17e, 15 and earlier. This needs a 20W or greater adapter.

A Qi2.2 charger still works on older iPhones, just at their lower speed. The iPhone 16e has no wireless charging at all ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**Android:**
- Few phones support Qi2. The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold do 15W, and the Pixel 10 Pro XL supports 25W Qi2.2.
- Samsung's Galaxy S26 lineup is "Qi2 Ready," which means it needs a magnetic case to use Qi2 chargers at up to 15W ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

**Buying tip:** Look for the official Qi2 or Qi2 25W logo, since only certified products can display it ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). "MagSafe-compatible" on a box is not the same as Qi2-certified.
